children: Gold edges higher amid cooling oil prices. However, stronger-than-expected U.S. data overnight is likely to limit the gains. U.S. job openings jumped to 7.52 million in September, well above the 7.1 million expected. The strong labor market demand is a hawkish surprise for the Federal Reserve, already debating a December hike, says Waleed Said, a technical analyst at GivTrade. The latest data is supportive of the dollar but another beat-down for gold, the analyst says. The focus now is on the midterm elections and Friday's non-farm payrolls, he adds. Spot gold is 0.2% higher at $3,936.44 an ounce. (sherry.qin@wsj.com)
